title: Single-Threaded Load Harness Reported as a Server Ceiling
pattern: A high-throughput server is benchmarked with a single-threaded (or otherwise fixed, small) client whose own CPU or connection capacity is never measured, and the plateau reached is reported as the server's limit.
why_bad: The client saturates its one core first and throughput levels off there. The resulting "scalability ceiling" is a property of the harness, leading to wrong capacity plans and wasted server-side tuning.
detection: A benchmark driver whose load loop runs on a single thread or connection with no option to scale client threads/processes, and no measurement of client CPU utilization, while results are reported as maximum server throughput.
counterexample: Latency micro-benchmarks of a single connection's protocol handling, where one client is the intended configuration and no throughput ceiling is claimed.
fix: Scale load generation across threads, processes or machines until adding client capacity no longer raises throughput, and record client CPU utilization to show the client stayed below saturation.
